body: This seems unreasonable to me. We can't determine where the signal is intended to be used, in the abstract class itself or in its descendants. For example, a warning about unused function parameters is not produced **only** for abstract methods, and not for all functions of the abstract class.

> This seems unreasonable to me. We can't determine where the signal is intended to be used, in the abstract class itself or in its descendants.

@dalexeev Understandable, I've edited my original post to add a use case and leave the actual solution up to discussion.

One alternate might be to allow:
```gdscript 
@abstract signal
```

Then you can determine the signal must be used by descendants.

Unfortunately, this has slightly different semantics. Abstract classes are incomplete classes that cannot be instantiated. Abstract methods are incomplete methods that prevent the containing class from completing. Your "abstract" signals, however, could very well exist in a concrete (complete) class.

Furthermore, unlike abstract methods, there is no mechanism for enforcing the use of an "abstract" signal in derived classes. GDScript only analyzes the current class and its dependencies, not all classes that inherit or depend on the current class.

That is, all you want is to suppress the warning and note that the signal is not used in this class, but rather in a derived class or even another class. But you can already do this with `@warning_ignore`.

An alternative approach is to use the signal in the current class. For example, the built-in `Resource` class has a `changed` signal and an `emit_changed()` method that emits it.

This is the simplest workaround and I was going to use this, but...

> 
> An alternative approach is to use the signal in the current class. For example, the built-in `Resource` class has a `changed` signal and an `emit_changed()` method that emits it.

You have just pointed me at the **perfect** fix to my particular use-case. I was making an abstract [blackboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackboard_system), extending a resource:

```gdscript
@abstract
class_name Blackboard
extends Resource

## Emitted when any property's value changes
signal updated

...
```
I was unaware a [built-in `changed` signal](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/classes/class_resource.html#class-resource-signal-changed) existed specifically for that purpose. Now I don't need to define a signal at all. 🙂
